title: find does not show which field or snippet matched
findings_note: dogfooding S15: slicer find lists matching items but not where the term hit (esp. body matches), so you re-open the slice to see why. Show the matched field + a short snippet in text and --json.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
`slicer find` (S15) lists matching items with the same rows as `list`, but never says where
the term hit. For a match that lives only in a slice body you must re-open the slice to see
why it matched — friction filed while dogfooding S15.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- src/slicer/cli.py: per-field matching in find (`_field_text`, `_find_match`, `_snippet`),
  replacing the single-blob `_search_text`.
- tests/test_find.py; README.md, docs/getting-started.md, docs/agents.md.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Search each requested field in scope order and report the first hit's field plus a one-line
snippet around it. Text output adds an indented `matched in <field>: <snippet>` line under
each item's existing row; `--json` adds `match: {field, snippet}` per result. The reported
field stays in the id/title/short_title/findings/body vocabulary and honours `--in`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
`slicer find <term>` shows the matched field and snippet; `--json` carries `match`; a
body-only term reports `body` with surrounding context; `--in` limits the reported field.
Focused find tests, the unit suite, slicer check, and git diff --check.
